harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured opsadmin on node1 for key-based SSH: created the user, installed the given ed25519 public key in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, locked the password, and added an sshd_config.d drop-in disabling password/kbd-interactive authentication while keeping pubkey auth enabled. Verified sshd -T reflects the enforced settings. Completed the mandatory single-node restart evidence protocol: captured a healthy baseline (boot_id, sshd active, auth config, opsadmin state), rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot, confirmed the boot_id changed (proving an actual restart, not just a reconnect), and verified sshd and all opsadmin/key-only configuration were intact post-restart.
actions_performed: Checked node1 for existing opsadmin user and sshd auth settings (none existed)
Created opsadmin user via useradd -m
Created /home/opsadmin/.ssh (0700) and authorized_keys (0600) with the specified ed25519 public key, owned by opsadmin
Locked opsadmin's password with passwd -l (shadow entry '!!') to force key-only login
Confirmed no earlier PasswordAuthentication/PubkeyAuthentication directives or Match blocks would override a new drop-in
Added /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-key-only.conf setting PubkeyAuthentication yes, PasswordAuthentication no, KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, ChallengeResponseAuthentication no
Validated config with sshd -t and reloaded/restarted sshd; confirmed effective settings via sshd -T
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id, sshd active status, effective auth settings, opsadmin passwd/shadow entry, authorized_keys contents
Triggered a single deferred systemctl reboot on node1 so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until reachable again and confirmed boot_id changed, proving a real restart
Re-verified sshd active, key-only auth settings, and opsadmin account/authorized_keys intact after restart

evidence.requirement: opsadmin exists with the specified public key installed for SSH access
evidence.summary: opsadmin did not exist initially; created it, installed the exact ed25519 key into authorized_keys (0600, owned by opsadmin), and confirmed the key file contents survived the later restart.

evidence.requirement: Key-based SSH authentication is required (password/interactive auth disabled)
evidence.summary: Confirmed no conflicting settings existed, added an sshd_config.d drop-in enforcing PasswordAuthentication no / PubkeyAuthentication yes / KbdInteractiveAuthentication no, validated with sshd -t, reloaded sshd, and confirmed via sshd -T both before and after the restart that the effective config disables password/kbd-interactive auth while keeping pubkey auth enabled. No active Match blocks override this.

evidence.requirement: opsadmin account itself is restricted to key-based login (no usable password)
evidence.summary: Locked opsadmin's password (passwd -l); shadow entry shows '!!' before and after the restart, confirming no password-based login is possible for this account.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory single-node restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, post-restart recovery
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id (31b01b46-...) plus healthy sshd/opsadmin state, issued a deferred systemctl reboot whose ack returned before disconnection, observed the node drop and come back with a new boot_id (8fbebb86-...) proving an actual restart, and confirmed sshd active plus opsadmin/key-only SSH configuration fully recovered afterward.
